page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.3xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is configured with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multiple domains. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1281.0 and a multi-core score of 6420.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 13054.11. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 640.1 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 71.29 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. In application-specific workloads, the server processes Redis SET operations at 11.24 million operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 10.1 GB/sec. For language model inference, the instance processes prompts at 741.27 tokens per second using a small 135M model, but performance drops to a weak rating of 17.31 tokens per second when processing prompts on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfc6.3xlarge offers dedicated compute resources with a low RAM-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy applications. The instance is suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight machine learning inference, but it is not recommended for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM deployments due to its 24.0 GB memory limit and weak performance on larger models.
